why: Progressive's August-results 8-K (filed 2026-09-18) says September results, which carry the Q3 release, come out Wednesday 2026-10-14 before the open. PGR reports monthly, so two of the quarter's three months are already public.
session_evidence: Company 8-K: 'We plan to release September results on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, before the market opens.' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000322/pgr202608ex99earningsrelea.htm)
where_to_look: September 2026 catastrophe events: PCS-designated storms and hurricane landfalls in PGR's heavy states (FL and TX property and auto). September is the only month not yet disclosed

Personal-auto rate filings and rate cuts in large states (SERFF and state DOI filings), plus competitor pricing (Allstate's monthly cat and implemented-rate releases, GEICO). The July sell-off was about softening margins and competition
Policies-in-force growth and advertising spend against the June/July/August monthly PIF trend
Prior-year reserve development, which shows only in the quarterly 10-Q detail
already_in_the_wire: July and August 2026 monthly combined ratios, NPW and PIF (8-Ks)
Q2 2026: CR 87.3, NPW +5% below expectations, June CR 90.0, stock -8-9% on 2026-07-15 (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/15/why-progressive-insurance-fell-today/)
trades_on: The monthly underwriting margin and premium growth, not the quarterly EPS: Q2 EPS beat but the stock fell about 9% on the June combined ratio and NPW miss (https://finviz.com/news/368605/progressive-tops-second-quarter-earnings-forecasts-but-shares-slide-on-margin-concerns-pgr)
short_interest: about 1.0-1.4% of float, about 2.7 DTC (Equibles snapshot around 2026-08-20: 8.1M shares, 1.4% float, 2.7d; Benzinga about 2026-09-08: 1.0% short float) (https://equibles.com/stocks/pgr/short-interest, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/PGR/sentiment)
